title: Stability Patterns after Bimaxillary Surgery in Patients with Skeletal Class III Malocclusion using OnyxCeph3TM: A Retrospective Cohort Study
summary: Following orthognathic surgery, the jaws occasionally shift back toward their preoperative positions; in some cases, this can affect the success of the treatment. To investigate stability patterns following this surgery, 38 patients were included, each of whom underwent lateral cephalometric radiography (LCR) before surgery and again immediately following a follow-up period of 6 to 9 months. Plaster models of the patients, which had been created for surgical planning, were also measured. Using these models, it is possible to determine by how much and in which directions the jaws were moved during surgery, as studies have shown this to be relevant for postoperative stability.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Patients at the Department of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery,
University Hospital Aachen
• Skeletal Angle Class III
• Underwent a bimaxillary repositioning osteotomy
for the first time
• Previously treated with orthodontics (decompensation)
Exclusion criteria:
• No developmental or syndromic conditions
such as cleft lip and palate
• Poor image quality of X-rays
• Patients who have undergone previous surgery or who have
experienced facial trauma
